name: Rujuta Diwekar
who: Postgraduate degree in Sports Science & Nutrition (SNDT College, Mumbai, 1999) plus Sports Dietitians training at the Australian Institute of Sport; longtime nutritionist to Bollywood stars and the Indian cricket team.
why: Set the template for mainstream Indian diet advice for two decades and reaches a bigger audience than almost any dietitian outside the anglosphere, without paid endorsements.

name: Pooja Makhija
who: BSc in Dietetics and MSc in Food Science & Nutrition; clinical nutritionist running a Mumbai practice for Bollywood clients and metabolic-health patients.
why: One of India's most visible clinical nutritionists, with an ongoing consulting practice and a bestselling book that shaped celebrity-diet coverage.

name: Carlos Ríos
who: Degree in Human Nutrition & Dietetics (Universidad Pablo de Olavide, Seville); registered dietista-nutricionista; founder of the Realfooding movement and MyRealFood app.
why: Built the biggest food-literacy movement in the Spanish-speaking world, a 4.5M-strong community, even as peer dietitians criticize its traffic-light simplifications.

name: Aitor Sánchez García
who: Dietista-Nutricionista and food technologist (Universidad de Alicante, with honors; Universidad de Granada); doctoral researcher who has worked at Sweden's Karolinska Institutet.
why: Runs both a clinical practice and 'Mi Dieta Cojea,' one of the most cited evidence-based nutrition outlets in the Spanish-speaking world.

name: Julio Basulto
who: Registered dietitian-nutritionist (colegiado CAT000943, Barcelona); editor of the Spanish Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics.
why: Decades of clinical practice paired with prolific myth-debunking books and talks that have shaped Spain's public nutrition debate.

name: Niko Rittenau
who: Bachelor's in nutrition counseling (DHfPG) and Master's in micronutrient therapy & regulation medicine (FHM Bielefeld); often billed as a 'nutritional scientist,' a label German media has called a stretch given his actual training.
why: Set the format for plant-based nutrition education in German-speaking Europe with a Spiegel-bestselling book, though he also runs a supplement business — a disclosed conflict of interest worth flagging.

name: Jean-Michel Cohen
who: MD and PhD in nutrition (Université Paris Diderot, 1983); runs the Savoir Maigrir coaching program and clinics out of Paris.
why: Forty years of French TV presence, a National Order of Merit for a food-labeling system, and a coaching program that scaled his practice to millions of dieters.
warning: France's medical board (Ordre des médecins) sanctioned Cohen in 2015 for advertising and commercial-practice violations tied to his nutrition program; the penalty was reduced to a fine on appeal in 2017.

name: Frédéric Saldmann
who: MD, dual-trained as a cardiologist and nutritionist, practicing out of Paris hospitals.
why: One of France's most consistent bestselling health authors, translating preventive-medicine research into mass-market nutrition advice for two decades.
reach: Multiple bestselling books; exact current social-media following unconfirmed (2026)

name: Frederico Lobo
who: MD with a registered nutrology specialization (CRM-GO 13192, RQE 11915), certified by ABRAN; practices in Goiânia, Brazil.
why: Helped found the Movimento Nutrologia Brasil in 2014 and built one of Brazil's most-watched physician-led nutrition YouTube channels.
reach: YouTube channel + Brazilian media presence; current subscriber count unconfirmed (2026)

name: Tim Noakes
who: MD and Professor Emeritus of Exercise & Sports Science, University of Cape Town; decades of research on carbohydrate and fat metabolism in endurance athletes.
why: Co-created the low-carb 'Banting' diet movement that reshaped South African eating habits, and was twice cleared of professional misconduct over his public advice.
reach: Legacy reach via bestselling books (The Real Meal Revolution) and the Banting-diet movement; current social following unconfirmed (2026)
warning: South Africa's health regulator (HPCSA) brought a professional-conduct case over his public low-carbohydrate infant-feeding advice in 2014; he was acquitted in 2017 and the regulator's appeal was dismissed in 2018.

name: Alberto Cormillot
who: MD (Universidad de Buenos Aires, 1961) with postgraduate training in Geneva; specializes in nutrition and obesity treatment.
why: Built Argentina's modern obesity-treatment infrastructure — clinics, self-help groups, and a foundation now active across several countries — over more than 60 years.

name: Iris Shai
who: PhD in nutrition and epidemiology, RD, MPH; professor at Ben-Gurion University and Reichman University, adjunct at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.
why: Her DIRECT and DIRECT-PLUS randomized trials reshaped the global low-carb-vs-Mediterranean-diet debate and guideline discussions, with 23,000-plus citations.
reach: Academic reach: 23,000+ citations; no major public social-media following (verified 2026-08)

name: Fan Zhihong
who: PhD in Food Science; professor and doctoral advisor at China Agricultural University, director at the China Nutrition Society.
why: China's most-followed nutrition science communicator, with a Weibo following in the millions and a role as the national science association's go-to nutrition voice.

name: Antonio Paoli
who: MD and Full Professor of Exercise & Sport Sciences, University of Padova; directs its Nutrition & Exercise Physiology Laboratory, with a second professorship at UCAM Murcia, Spain.
why: One of the most-cited researchers on ketogenic diets and athletic performance, with a body of work widely applied in sports-nutrition practice.
reach: Academic reach: ~21K citations, h-index 48; minimal public social-media following (verified 2026-08)
